# SparLab result tables

**Generated file - do not edit by hand.** Refresh with `make results` after a benchmark run.

## Verification and validation

Generated by `python/scripts/write_result_tables.py` from `results/verification/summary.json`. Verification compares against exact answers for the discrete problem; validation compares against an independent theory, where a finite gap is expected.

| study                                                      | kind                      | metric                                                   | value     | tolerance | result |
|------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------|-----------|-----------|--------|
| patch test (constant strain, distorted mesh)               | verification              | max relative error in u, strain and stress               | 4.066e-15 | 1e-10     | PASS   |
| solver agreement (sparse vs dense)                         | verification              | max relative displacement difference vs dense LU         | 7.038e-12 | 1e-08     | PASS   |
| sensitivity (analytical vs central differences)            | verification              | min over steps of max relative error                     | 2.177e-08 | 1e-05     | PASS   |
| mesh convergence (cantilever tip deflection)               | verification + validation | relative error vs Timoshenko on the finest mesh (nu = 0) | 0.0004781 | 0.02      | PASS   |
| modal frequencies (cantilever vs Euler-Bernoulli)          | validation                | f1 relative error on the finest mesh                     | 0.005522  | 0.02      | PASS   |
| patch test 3-D (constant strain, distorted Hex8 mesh)      | verification              | max relative error in u, strain and stress               | 1.626e-15 | 1e-10     | PASS   |
| sensitivity 3-D (analytical vs central differences, Hex8)  | verification              | min over steps of max relative error                     | 1.555e-08 | 1e-05     | PASS   |
| mesh convergence 3-D (Hex8 cantilever tip deflection)      | verification + validation | relative error vs Timoshenko on the finest mesh          | 0.005415  | 0.03      | PASS   |
| modal frequencies 3-D (Hex8 cantilever vs Euler-Bernoulli) | validation                | f1 (weak axis) relative error on the finest mesh         | 0.01063   | 0.03      | PASS   |

## Cross-validation against independent codes

Generated from `results/cross_validation/summary.json` by `python/scripts/cross_validate.py`: node-by-node comparison of the nodal displacements with scikit-fem (same element formulation) and CalculiX (C3D8 is the same element; CPS4 is a plane element CalculiX expands through the thickness). CalculiX results are read from its .frd output, which carries six significant digits, so differences below 5e-6 relative are its rounding.

| block_3d_analysis   | Hex8            | top_pressure | scikit-fem 12.0.2 | ElementHex1       | 1.42e-11     | 7.27e-12     | 1e-07     | PASS   |

## Stress-constrained optimisation

The constraint bounds the relaxed (rho^q) von Mises stress aggregated with a scaled p-norm; `max relaxed ratio` is the true relaxed maximum over the limit at the returned design, and `re-solve max vM` is the peak von Mises of the thresholded structure analysed as solid material, which is the number that says whether the structure meets the limit. The `constraint off` row is the same deck run with the constraint disabled.

| case                              | constraint | limit [Pa] | compliance [J] | max relaxed ratio | p-norm ratio | p-norm scale | feasible | re-solve max vM [Pa] | re-solve / limit | iterations |
|-----------------------------------|------------|------------|----------------|-------------------|--------------|--------------|----------|----------------------|------------------|------------|
| l_bracket_stress                  | on         | 9400000    | 0.0900601      | 0.98296           | 1.1804       | 0.84211      | yes      | 7.507e+06            | 0.7986           | 240        |
| l_bracket_stress (constraint off) | off        | 9400000    | 0.0852764      | n/a               | n/a          | n/a          | n/a      | 1.0135e+07           | 1.078            | 115        |

## Runtime scaling (3-D, Hex8)

Same protocol on a Hex8 block (nx x nx/2 x nx/4 cells). The direct solver's fill-in grows much faster in 3-D, which is what limits the solid problem size.
